verdict: In its first quarter as a standalone company after spinning off Aerospace, Honeywell Technologies grew organic sales 7%, expanded operating margin to 14.8%, and raised its full-year outlook.

segments.name: Building Automation
segments.note: Fire, security and controls for buildings — products grew 11% on fire and security demand.

segments.name: Process Automation and Technology
segments.note: Automation and process technology for energy and industry; project sales grew 14% on LNG and petrochemical work.

segments.name: Industrial Automation
segments.note: Sensing, measurement and warehouse automation. Reported sales fell 23% because two businesses were sold in the quarter, but underlying (organic) sales grew 4%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new products across automation and technology.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, head office and the cost of running a newly standalone company.

otherDetail: Other income of $389M (including a $339M gain on selling non-strategic businesses), less $143M of interest and financial charges, a $147M equity loss, and a $103M loss from discontinued operations — the spun-off Aerospace business — net −$4M.
footerNote: Net income of $676M is the total; $664M was attributable to Honeywell Technologies shareholders after noncontrolling interests. This is the first quarter reported on the post-spin perimeter, with Aerospace shown as discontinued operations.

takeaways.title: Segment profit jumped
takeaways.text: Segment profit rose 23% to $1,062 million and segment margin expanded to 21.3%, helped by productivity, pricing, and eliminating stranded costs left over from earlier spin-offs and sales.

takeaways.title: Backlog near $19 billion
takeaways.text: Backlog grew 7% year over year to nearly $19 billion (excluding the two businesses sold in the quarter), and management raised full-year guidance: sales of $20.0–20.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $8.40–8.45.

takeaways.title: Industrial Automation shrank — on paper
takeaways.text: Reported Industrial Automation sales fell 23%, but that is the sale of the warehouse (WWS) and productivity (PSS) businesses leaving the numbers; the remaining business grew 4% organically and its margin expanded 3.5 points to 18.4%.

oneTimers: First quarter as a standalone company following the Honeywell Aerospace spin-off (completed June 29, 2026): Aerospace results sit in discontinued operations, which lost $103M in the quarter.
Other income includes a $339M gain on selling non-strategic businesses and assets, and the quarter absorbed $94M of divestiture-related costs.
Reported EPS from continuing operations fell 20% only because the year-ago quarter contained a one-time gain from the Resideo termination agreement; adjusted EPS rose 34%.
